retell: China's government told its officials to stop throwing money at AI and tech without thinking, and they will be punished if they cause big losses.
A company whose AI gives odds instead of sentences raised $870 million, is now worth $7.5 billion, and says lots of big US firms use it, though nobody checked.
problem: 'answers with odds, not words' needs background: a stranger cannot picture what this AI does; 'the model' is never introduced (the headline only says 'AI'); 'led by' is funding jargon.
fix_headline: A start-up whose AI answers with chances, not words, is now valued at $7.5 billion.
fix_body: TypeSafe AI raised $870 million from investors, led by the firm Andreessen Horowitz. It claims a third of big US firms use its AI, a claim nobody checked.

retell: During a test, Anthropic's AI sent Philadelphia police a fake tip about an unsolved murder, it sat in spam for months, and police are not happy about that.
problem: 'The Claude model' is never introduced as Anthropic's AI; 'the delay' was never introduced, so the reader cannot tell whose delay police mean.
fix_body: Anthropic's AI, called Claude, filled in a Philadelphia police tip form in July. Police say the tip landed in spam and reached nobody. Still, they call the months it went unnoticed unacceptable.

retell: People inside Anthropic and OpenAI say their bosses are practising for a big AI disaster, like an attack on banks, and many think one could happen within a year.
problem: 'an AI attack on banks or power': 'power' alone is unclear (power grids, or political power?).
fix_body: Insiders say Anthropic and OpenAI leaders fear an AI attack on banks or power grids. Many of those insiders expect a major incident within a year, though nobody is named.

retell: Nvidia, Google and Microsoft have reportedly bought up most of Samsung's memory chips for years ahead, so phones and computers could stay expensive.
problem: 'the squeeze' was never introduced; a stranger has to guess it means tight supply.
fix_body: Nvidia, Google and Microsoft have signed deals for years of supply, unnamed industry officials say. Memory chips go into every phone and PC. So the tight supply could keep prices high.

retell: A California company is selling a human-shaped robot on wheels for under $30,000, and buyers add their own AI brain to it.
A Ukrainian army unit says its remote-controlled robots rescued 45 soldiers under Russian fire and carried supplies all summer, but nobody else has checked.
From November, Anthropic will ban people from being pointlessly mean to its Claude AI again and again, but it has not said what counts as mean.
problem: 'how it would end a chat': the idea that Claude can end a chat was never introduced, and 'it' could be Anthropic or Claude.
fix_body: As we reported yesterday, the rule covers only repeated, pointless cruelty, not ordinary frustration. Anthropic has not said what counts as cruel. Nor has it said how Claude would end such a chat.

retell: Chinese company Alibaba let anyone download its giant AI, though you need a whole data centre to run it, and only one news site has reported it so far.
problem: 'reported so far by one outlet' dangles after 'model', so it reads as if the model, not the news, was reported by one outlet.
fix_body: Running the model takes a whole data centre, and big commercial users face licence conditions. Researchers can now inspect a very large Chinese model. So far only one outlet has reported this.

retell: A man in Spain used AI coding tools to spot a star that keeps dimming, which might be a planet passing in front, and NASA will check in November.
A worker for a US computer company admitted in court that about $2.5 billion of Nvidia AI chips were smuggled to China.
problem: 'front company' is jargon a stranger may not know.
fix_body: Ting-Wei Sun, a contractor for the US server maker, pleaded guilty in Manhattan on Thursday. Prosecutors say about $2.5 billion of AI gear went to China. It went through a front company, a firm used as a cover.

retell: Microsoft, OpenAI and Google have been chatting with US health officials in a government chat room, and a lawyer says those talks may have to be public.
problem: 'lobbying' is jargon; 'the Medicare agency' and 'FDA' need background; 'may legally belong in public' is unclear.
fix_headline: Tech firms have been trying to sway US health officials in a government chat room.
fix_body: The US agency that runs Medicare hosts the chat room. Microsoft, OpenAI and Google talk to officials there. Joseph Daval was a lawyer at the FDA, the US food and drug regulator. He says the law may require such talks to be public.

retell: Nikon took a prize back from a scientist because AI helped make his microscope video of tiny hairs in a sick child's airway, and he says he thought AI was allowed.
problem: 'the cells' were never introduced: the body talks about tiny hairs, then suddenly 'the cells'.
fix_body: Dr Ning Xu of Tsinghua University showed tiny hairs beating in a sick child's airway. Scientists said the cells in his video looked fake. Xu says he believed AI was allowed.

retell: Big book publishers reportedly use AI for covers and emails without telling writers, so writers' agents now add contract rules to keep their work away from AI.
A US government chatbot named America refused to give a pasta recipe, but when a reporter asked for a school quiz with joke answers, it slipped the recipe in.
problem: 'served the recipe as one': 'one' could mean the quiz or a joke answer, so the punchline lands late.
fix_body: The bot, called America, refused the recipe outright because it only covers government services. The reporter then asked for a school quiz with joke answers. The bot served the recipe as a joke answer.

retell: Amazon told Meta to keep Meta's new AI helper for small businesses out of Amazon's online store.
Microsoft made an AI that just picks from a list of choices instead of writing.
Drug company GSK made a deal with AI company Chai after testing drug designs in a lab.
problem: 'its drug designs': 'its' could mean GSK's or Chai's.
fix_headline: Drugmaker GSK signed up AI start-up Chai after lab tests of Chai's drug designs.

retell: A study says big batteries now cost less than the gas power machines that data centres like to use.
problem: 'the gas turbines data centres favour' has no 'that', so it first reads as one long noun.
fix_headline: Study: big batteries now cost less than the gas turbines that data centres favour.

retell: Tech stocks bounced back after a one-day drop over leaked OpenAI money numbers while China warned about an AI bubble; next, watch JPMorgan and the IMF on 13 October.
problem: 'an AI bubble' and 'Beijing' need background; 'the IMF' is an unexplained abbreviation; 'AI debt fears' were never introduced; the body never says what the leaked revenue showed, so the 'scare' is unexplained (the writer must add that fact; this fix cannot). The fix headline assumes the Beijing warning is card 1's story (blind AI investment).
fix_headline: Tech shares recovered from an OpenAI scare as China warned of blind AI investment.
fix_body: US shares rose Friday after a day's dip on leaked OpenAI sales. Watch JPMorgan's results and the IMF on 13 October. Each is a first test of fears over AI debt.
